 Jackson County supervisors call for changes after Election Day voting delays 
 Jackson County Supervisor Ken Taylor said the county’s Election Day voting process was “a serious problem” that “we should not be allowing… to happen.” By Will Polston Published : Nov. 16, 2026 at 6:32 PM CST | Updated : 14 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google JACKSON COUNTY, Miss. (WLOX) — Jackson County Supervisor Ken Taylor said the county’s Election Day voting process was “a serious problem” that “we should not be allowing… to happen.”
 Taylor said many voters waited hours to cast a ballot, were held up by a lack of machines and felt like they were being watched while voting.
 Taylor said a disagreement between election commission President Danny Glaskox and other county election officials could have contributed to the delays.
 “He was recommending to the other commissioners that we have more machines on site and they said no,” Taylor said. “There’s an internal problem that needs to be fixed.”
 The supervisors agreed something had to be done.
 Supervisor Randy Bosarge said the pay of election commissioners has caused issues in the past. The position is scheduled for only a few hours a day, but most commissioners work past those hours without compensation to make sure elections are done right, according to the report.
 The board as a whole voiced support to help where it can.
 “I want to help them get more money. I want to help them get more hours. I want to help them to where we don’t have this situation again,” Bosarge said.
 Taylor suggested the board meet with the election commission to see what issues the board can help with. He said improvement is needed before the next election.
